goal: Reference implementation of BIP460 Cross-Input Signature Aggregation for Taproot key-path spends, letting multiple Taproot inputs share one aggregated signature.
Companion draft commits also add descriptor and PSBT support so wallets can prototype coinjoin/payjoin-style use cases on top of it.
reviewability: Marked needs-rebase and mergeable_state is dirty, so the tip is not currently mergeable against master.
Author explicitly asked reviewers to focus on the core consensus/policy commits, not the later draft-bip wallet/PSBT commits which are expected to keep changing.
agreement: Author frames this explicitly as a draft to accompany unmerged BIPs, not intended for merge (fjahr).

A first substantive review found three concrete correctness bugs in the wallet/PSBT signing and finalization paths, including cases where testmempoolaccept fails after signrawtransactionwithwallet reports complete=true (BarneyChambers).
No author response yet, posted one day before assessment.

result.summary: This PR is a reference implementation of BIP460 (Cross-Input Signature Aggregation for Taproot key-path spends), adding a new witness v2 output type whose spends can be aggregated via BIP458 half-aggregation or BIP459 full-aggregation, or spent individually with a plain BIP341 signature. It touches consensus deployment, script verification, policy, PSBT, wallet signing, RPC, and vendors two experimental unmerged secp256k1 modules (halfagg, fullagg) via subtree update. Later commits (prefixed draft-bip) go further, adding companion descriptor (cisa()/rawcisa()) and PSBT field/role support that the author says are unreviewed drafts included only so others can prototype end-to-end. Activation is regtest-only; there is no deployment on any other network.
result.problem: There is currently no way to aggregate signatures across multiple Taproot inputs in a transaction, which second-layer protocols like payjoin and coinjoin could use to reduce transaction size and cost. This PR gives the BIP process and interested developers a concrete, runnable implementation to review and prototype against, ahead of any decision on whether BIP460 should be adopted.

open_concerns: signrawtransactionwithwallet can report complete=true for a v2 input that is actually an incomplete aggregation-group member, only caught later by mempool policy (BarneyChambers, unaddressed).
combinepsbt silently keeps whichever half-agg signature it sees first when two PSBTs disagree, unlike the full-agg path which already detects this conflict (BarneyChambers, unaddressed).

finalizepsbt can build a second, invalid aggregation group when one input in a group is already finalized and another is added later, causing consensus to reject the transaction with SCRIPT_ERR_CISA_GROUP_INVALID (BarneyChambers, unaddressed).

reviewability.label: Needs rebase
reviewability.reason: Labeled Needs rebase with mergeable_state dirty, a mechanical blocker independent of the draft-bip design questions. The author has also asked reviewers to focus on the core consensus/policy commits rather than the still-evolving draft-bip wallet/PSBT commits.

agreement.reason: A real, substantive review surfaced three unresolved correctness issues (mis-reported completeness, PSBT combine losing conflicting signatures, invalid aggregation groups from finalize) that the reviewer frames as suggestions rather than explicit blockers, and the author has not had a chance to respond (posted one day before this assessment).

categories.rationale: P3 because a reviewer already surfaced concrete correctness problems that would affect fund safety if this shipped (a supposedly complete signature that mempool rejects, combinepsbt silently dropping a conflicting half-agg signature, and finalize producing consensus-invalid aggregation groups), but the feature itself is explicitly experimental and not slated for merge.

uncertainties: Whether the draft-bip descriptor/PSBT commits should be weighed the same as the core consensus/policy commits for priority purposes, given the author asked reviewers to set them aside; I included them since membership is inclusive of what the diff touches.
No maintainer area labels beyond 'Needs rebase' were given, so category membership for validation/wallet/mempool/rpc/utils rests on diff inspection rather than a labeled prior.
Long-term significance of BIP458/459/460 within the BIP process is outside this PR's discussion and not something I can assess from the given signals.
result.card: BIP460: CISA for Taproot key path spends is a reference implementation of cross-input signature aggregation for Taproot key-path spends, adding a new witness v2 output type, half/full aggregation modes, PSBT and wallet support, plus a secp256k1 subtree bump vendoring two experimental, not-yet-merged upstream crypto modules. The author explicitly states this is 'a draft to accompany the BIPs, not intended for merge' and activation is regtest-only. A reviewer (BarneyChambers) who built and tested the branch found three concrete bugs: signrawtransactionwithwallet reporting complete=true for signatures that mempool then rejects, combinepsbt silently dropping a conflicting half-agg signature, and finalizepsbt producing consensus-invalid aggregation groups; the author has not yet responded. The PR is labeled Needs rebase with a dirty mergeable state. No dependency on other open PRs was stated, but it depends on two unmerged secp256k1 PRs (#1566, #1754) for the vendored crypto modules.
